name: Session and controller manager
purpose: Own controller identity and generation, bounded live-session capacity, handle issuance, and the single ordered validation path (handle, context, time, action) that precedes every mutation.
responsibilities: Register a host-issued, globally unique controller identity under a host-provided controller name, within a host-supplied, non-zero uniqueness scope that is bound into every handle; track superseded controller identities in a bounded window to recognize recreated controllers, and never derive identity from a per-manager counter.
Consume a permit exactly once and bind it to a new session, validating the runtime SessionContext against the permit field-by-field and reporting the mismatching field locator.

Issue opaque handles binding the manager uniqueness scope, controller identity, generation, and session identity; validate the scope first so a foreign or recreated manager's handle is rejected before any session is addressed.
Apply the declared diagnostic precedence (handle, context, time, action, quota, capacity) and guarantee that no state mutates when any validation fails.

Resolve every time-dependent decision through the owned time authority (never a direct comparison of the caller's claim): obtain the authority's reading in the claim domain, cross-check the caller's claim against it, map to the validity domain when needed, and only then test the validity interval.
Bound live sessions by a host-configured capacity; a failed creation returns no handle and frees its slot exactly on terminal/closed reclamation.
Expose a zero normal-route emission counter that remains zero and no emission, transport, journal, or persistence API.
state_ownership: Host-supplied, non-zero uniqueness scope (ManagerScope) required at construction and bound into every issued handle; distinct per manager instance and per recreation.
Controller table (controller id -> generation, name) with a bounded superseded-controller window.
Live session table bounded by max_sessions; each entry binds a session, its permit identity, and the owning controller id/generation.
A single std::mutex guarding all manager state; the manager is non-copyable and non-movable.
interfaces: consume(ControllerId, const Permit&, const SessionContext&, SessionHandle& out) -> Result
transition(SessionHandle, LifecycleAction, ClockDomainId now_domain, Timestamp now_value, Diagnostic& out) -> Result
capacity() const -> std::size_t; emission_count() const -> std::uint64_t (always zero)
concurrency: All operations take the single std::mutex; concurrent consumes and transitions serialize deterministically, and exactly-once consumption holds under concurrency via the registry's atomic check-then-insert.
errors: InvalidHandle, ForeignHandle, StaleHandle, RecreatedController, SessionNotFound, InvalidController (zero or duplicate controller identity at registration).
UnknownClock, MissingMapping, ToleranceExceeded, ClockRegression, ClockOverflow, ClockSourceFailure, ClockOutOfBounds, PermitNotYetValid, PermitExpired.
UndefinedAction, ActionNotAllowed, InvalidTransition, TerminalState, QuotaExhausted, AlreadyApplied.
deployment: Compiled in the standalone candidate; it is the only entry point tests drive end-to-end, so no transport, gateway, or journal type is ever instantiated.
rationale: A single facade enforces the required validation-before-mutation ordering in one place and keeps the handle/controller/generation trust boundary coherent, making stale, foreign, and recreated-handle rejection deterministic.
